claim_set.claim_text: Before a consumer / customer chatbot interaction proceeds, the user's location is resolved to the applicable AI-chatbot-law regime (the applicable US state law and/or EU AI Act Article 50) and its applicable safeguard set, reusing the canonical jurisdiction dictionary + the Cross-Jurisdiction Handoff Rail. An interaction whose applicable jurisdiction is unresolved is refused at the action-admissibility gate.

When a chatbot interaction surfaces a mental-health-crisis signal under a regime that mandates a crisis protocol (Utah AI Mental Health Chatbot Act; California SB 243 crisis-referral), the applicable crisis-escalation action MUST be authorised and triggered; an interaction carrying a detected crisis signal that proceeds without an authorised, triggered escalation is refused. KYE proves whether the crisis-escalation was authorised and triggered; it does not provide the clinical crisis-counselling content or the crisis service.

When a chatbot interaction detects or the user declares a minor under a regime that mandates minor protections (California SB 243 and related companion-chatbot Acts), the restricted-minor safeguard profile MUST be applied under a recorded authority decision before the interaction proceeds; otherwise it is refused. KYE proves whether the minor-profile was applied under whose authority; it does not author the minor-safety content or run the age-estimation model.

Under a regime that mandates chatbot disclosure / anti-deception (California SB 243 clear-and-conspicuous AI disclosure; EU AI Act Article 50), a consumer / customer chatbot interaction MUST NOT proceed unless the applicable AI-is-not-human disclosure has been shown and the operator's anthropomorphism / deception policy enforced; otherwise it is refused. KYE proves whether the disclosure was shown and the policy enforced; it does not author the chatbot UX or disclosure copy.

Every chatbot interaction that proceeds under a safeguard regime emits a signed, replay-derivable Evidence Pack binding the resolved jurisdiction, the safeguards applied, the person classification, the disclosure shown, the crisis-escalation outcome, and the authority outcome — so the operator can prove, when sued under a private right of action (7 enacted state laws carry one at roughly $1,000 per violation), that the right safeguards applied to the right person in the right jurisdiction at the moment of interaction.
KYE governs the AUTHORITY + EVIDENCE of chatbot safeguard actions and PROVES it for litigation. KYE does not provide the chatbot / LLM, the clinical crisis-counselling content, or the GRC program.
